records.supported_name_scope: Churchill River is supported as the representative identity of this drainage collection. The modeled mainstem includes a southwestern feeder and lake chain, Atikonak River, Ossokmanuan reservoir passage, the Unknown River/Twin Falls outlet corridor, and the lower Churchill corridor. These are not all named Churchill River. No uppermost feeder name, lake-passage river name, exact name-transition vertex or uniform name for the 16 fragments is assigned.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The four actual cached mainstem pieces were read together with the wider northern and western group context. Their southwestern lake-chain detour, northward Atikonak approach, Ossokmanuan outlet turn, Churchill valley bends, Winokapau passage and eastern coastal ending distinguish this Labrador system from other rivers named Churchill.
records.region: Western and central Labrador, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada, extending from the Lac Joseph drainage to the Churchill outlet near Happy Valley-Goose Bay and Lake Melville.
records.completion_scope: Representative-system identity only. Independent readable evidence is sufficient despite several unavailable optional maps; no additional acquisition is pending for this bounded finding. Individual reach naming would be separate work.

naming_scope_details.unassigned: Initial southwestern feeder, individual lake-chain connections, exact lake entry/exit vertices, precise name transitions, tributary names and the generalized mouth channel.
naming_scope_details.historical_name_limit: No Hamilton River alias or naming-date claim is established by this finding.

records.supported_name_scope: The upper selected route follows the Fiambalá/Saujil–Abaucán–Salado/Colorado corridor, but the complete modeled group continues beyond the mapped river termination through the Salina La Antigua setting and into Salinas Grandes. Neither one river name nor the equivalence of those salt-flat connections to a named natural river is established for all three pieces.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Northwestern Argentina, from the northern Fiambalá valley in Catamarca through Tinogasta and the southern edge of the Pipanaco depression, then the Mazán corridor and Llanos de La Rioja, followed by a long southern/eastern modeled extension to Salinas Grandes on the La Rioja–Córdoba side. Distinct from the Bermejo/Vinchina drainage to the west and the Belén–Salar de Pipanaco drainage to the east of the upper valley.
records.completion_scope: Completed full-selected-route geographical and naming-scope assessment. The hold is caused by the composite river/salt-flat/model-link scope, not missing source access. Future resolution of a scalar name, a system display label or reach splitting would require a separately authorized naming decision; no further acquisition is required now to establish the hold.

records.supported_name_scope: No natural river name is established for the complete representative modeled MAIN_RIV path. This is a completed northern Inland Ice to northeastern ice-margin and fjord-head naming scope hold, not a statement that every marginal stream is unnamed.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Northern Greenland Inland Ice, followed eastward toward the ice-margin and ice-free corridor south of Mylius-Erichsen Land and the inner Danmark Fjord approach. Mylius-Erichsen Land and Danmark Fjord are geographic reference labels, not river names assigned to the group.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Keep the saved order unchanged and use later result IDs/status changes to mark progress. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated; no lake research until all river continental phases have had their review pass.
